summary: Directory lists a removed Francis Marion National Forest tower at Buck Hall. No source dates it or describes what remains; a National Forest Foundation guide describes a campground there.

facts.status_note: Listed as Removed in the directory. No source found gives a removal date or describes what remains.

evidence.supports: Directory places the Buck Hall tower in Charleston County, within Francis Marion National Forest
evidence.quote: South Carolina - Charleston County - Francis Marion National Forest

evidence.supports: Directory marks the Buck Hall tower as removed
Forest Service once had more than a dozen lookout stations in the forest
evidence.quote: Originally, there were more than a dozen such stations.

evidence.supports: Two Forest Service lookout towers still standing, Witherbee being one
evidence.quote: Witherbee is one of two Forest Service lookout towers in the Francis Marion Forest still standing

evidence.supports: Witherbee tower built in the 1930s at another site, moved to the ranger district office in 1952
evidence.quote: The tower originally was built at another location nearby in the 1930s and moved to the Witherbee Ranger District Office in 1952.

evidence.supports: Forest Service used the Witherbee tower until 1989
evidence.quote: The Forest Service used it until 1989.

evidence.supports: Buck Hall Recreation Area offers water, tent camping, showers and a picnic shelter
evidence.quote: There is water, tent camping, showers, and a picnic shelter

evidence.supports: Buck Hall Recreation Area is situated on the Intracoastal Waterway
Campground sits on the site of the former Buck Hall Plantation
evidence.quote: Buck Hall sits on top of where Buck Hall Plantation once stood

notes_for_editor: Only the directory names a tower at Buck Hall; the other sources describe the forest's towers in general, and the Witherbee tower in the Post and Courier article is a different tower. The Post and Courier article is undated in the copy I read. A search snippet mentioned a 315 ft SBA Towers registry structure in Buck Hall; that is a communications tower, not a lookout, and is not cited. The NFF guide's Honey Hill entry describes an old fire tower, no longer in use, at a different campground; a possible source of mix-up, not used.
